Host Guide

Getting the most out of Alfred

From adding your first property to what your guests actually experience — plus answers to the questions hosts ask most.

One thing you'll see before Step 1: the first time you log in with no properties yet, Alfred shows this exact walkthrough on screen — so if you lose this page, the app will remind you where you left off.

1

Create your account

Sign up with your email and a password. This becomes your host login — the one place you'll manage every property and every guest conversation.

2

Add your property

From your dashboard, add a property and paste in its Airbnb listing URL. Alfred reads the public listing automatically — amenities, house rules, description, photos — so you don't have to retype anything that's already public.

3

Upload what Alfred should know

The listing alone won't cover everything a guest asks at 11pm. Add anything that fills the gaps — the more specific, the better Alfred's answers.

Gold for Alfred
  • Past guest conversations — an Airbnb message export, or just your longest threads
  • A voice note for anything hands-on — towels, linens, the washer, how guests get in
  • A voice note about a past complaint or escalation — what happened and how you'd want it handled next time
  • A video walkthrough of the property (coming soon — not yet supported)
Also helps
  • Your house manual or welcome-book
  • A photo of the WiFi router — name + password
  • How your appliances work — thermostat, washer, coffee machine
  • Check-in / check-out steps and house rules
  • Parking or building access notes
  • Your automated or saved-reply templates, if you already use them
  • Extra photos of specific details the public Airbnb photos don't show

Whatever's easiest — photo, PDF, document, or just tell me in a voice note.

4

Train Alfred

Tap TRAIN NOW and Alfred reads everything you uploaded, then merges it with the listing into one knowledge base — no extra steps.

If something disagrees If your files and the listing conflict on a detail — say, a different WiFi password — Alfred will flag it and ask you which one is correct before finishing training. Pick the right answer for each, and Alfred takes it from there.
That's it. Once trained, Alfred handles guest messages on autopilot — you'll only be pulled in when something genuinely needs a human.

Training isn't a one-time step. Tap Details on any property card to keep Alfred current, any time.

Overview

Status, your Airbnb link, and a language setting — send the welcome message in English too, alongside the local language. Also shows how many files Alfred has on record; tap Manage to add more and retrain any time.

Knowledge

The most hands-on tab — three ways to shape what Alfred knows:

  • Add New Knowledge — type, or record a voice note, to add or correct a detail. Updates immediately, no re-ingest needed.
  • Automated Learning — review Q&A pairs Alfred drafts from resolved guest escalations. Accept adds them to the permanent Vault, Discard drops them.
  • Ask the Knowledge Base — chat directly with Alfred to see exactly what he'd tell a guest, without waiting for a real one to ask.
1

Generate a guest link

Tap + Guest on the property card to create a link for a guest — real or a test booking. Fill in a name and hit Generate Link to create real links you can use to message Alfred yourself, as a guest.

2

Choose how to send it

You have up to three ways to reach your guest — web chat, WhatsApp, or Telegram. Send whichever you or your guest prefers.

  • Guest link (web)
  • Guest link (WhatsApp)
  • Guest link (Telegram)

No matter which one you send, it's the same Alfred answering — already briefed on this specific property and this guest's booking dates.

Coming soon Native Airbnb inbox integration is in development. Until it rolls out, sharing one of the links above is how a guest reaches Alfred.
3

Always know who and where

Alfred's live Host Chat view always shows the header for that guest's conversation — the property and who's booked, at a glance.

4

Same links, right here too

Handy to resend without leaving this view.

5

Autopilot handles it — until it needs you

Alfred handles a conversation on its own by default. Watch what happens when a guest asks something it's not fully confident about →

6

Escalated — flagged for you

Alfred switches to Intervene automatically whenever something needs your OK, or anything it's not confident about. You can also flip to Intervene yourself anytime, escalation or not.

7

Your turn

Alfred drafts a reply for you — hit Send first. Once it's sent, click Mark Issue as Resolved so Alfred can resume control — resolving before the guest actually has an answer would leave them hanging.

8

All yours again

Once resolved, Alfred resumes handling the conversation itself. Questions along the way? Check the FAQ below. Want to run through everything again sometime? This guide is always here.

9

See it from both sides

Now go use the test links you already generated — open your preferred channel link and talk to Alfred as if you were the guest, and see both sides in action.

A minute or two for most properties. Larger uploads (many files or photos) can take a bit longer — Alfred saves progress as it goes, so if something times out, retrying only reprocesses what's still outstanding, not everything from scratch.

Open the property's Knowledge tab and use Add New Knowledge to correct it directly — no re-upload or retraining needed, it updates immediately.

Alfred escalates the conversation to you instead of guessing. You'll see it flagged in your dashboard and can reply directly — see the Guest Experience tab for more.

No — only new or changed files get processed on the next Train Now. Anything already trained is skipped automatically.

Alfred flags the conflict and asks you to pick which is correct before finishing training — it never silently guesses.

Yes — train your property once and it's available on all three channels automatically, no separate setup per channel.

PDF, DOCX, images, spreadsheets, and voice notes — up to 15MB per file.

See something confusing, or found a bug? Use the feedback icon in the dashboard — top right, next to your profile — any time.
